As the media tells people to stop criticizing Newton, they should remember that they created the controversy {my thoughts on the article in the comments)

The sentiment in this article is the same as you'll find in many opinion pieces in the sports pages around the country right now: Cam gets extra criticism for celebrating because he's black.

I'v discussed why this is stupid before so I won't go into to it here unless someone wants to go down that discussion path again. Today I'd like to point out the hypocrisy in the media of saying his celebrations should be enjoyed. Celebrations are nothing new. We've gone through the ever expanding rules that penalize celebrations for more than a decade. This has for the most part been cheerled by the media. Every sports commentator with a microphone of a computer extolled how players should be more like Emmett Smith and act like they'd been in the end zone before and less like Joe Horn or Ochocinco with their choreographed celebrations. Some will remember the Cowboys-9ers game in 2000 where the media actually backed the Cowboys taking an after the whistle cheap shot on Terrell Owens for doing a midfield celebration after a TD:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K-nxdzgQH8U

Yet here now we have Cam Newton, a man who poses after routine first downs, causing the media to run to his defense and cry that, "He's just having fun," and that those who do't appreciate that at best don't get it and at worst are bigots. I'd love these outlets that led the charge in criticizing guys like TO to explain to me how Newton's celebrations are different and should be appreciated? Some might say Cam isn't stashing cellphones in the end zone of sombreros on the sideline or the like, so it is more spontaneous and in fun.This might be a reasonable line of thought if Newton's celebrations were ever spontaneous. But when you pose after every first down, and do a set dance in the end zone it's no more spontaneous than stashing a Sharpee in your sock.

Reasonable people can disagree on the extent celebrations should be allowed, accepted or embraced in the NFL. Some people may want any and all celebrations banned in the name of professionalism and being sportsmanship role models. Others may argue that even taunting shouldn't be a penalty because at the end of the day it's a game made for entertainment only and celebrations are entertaining. Me, I'm somewhere int he middle and like celebrations, but prefer players who keep them for the biggest plays and don't break them out on routine first downs. If guys like Newton want to pose after plays that aren't game changers, okay, I'm not calling for a penalty on it or the like, but I don't have to cheer it and am free to cite that as a reason I don't particularly care to cheer for the player. And I'd love for someone in the media to explain why I "don't get it" for holding a more liberal view celebrations than most of them have for the past two decades just because I haven't ordained Cam Newton as my favorite football player.
